claim: The chapter's verb rule (the casual present affirmative is the dictionary form, いきます becomes いく) is shown in sentences but stated on no shipping card in either unit.
evidence: Book, Sample Dialogue 2: 'いきます。 → いく。 The present affirmative form of verbs is expressed by the dictionary form.' The base card that stated it (chapter-25/verb-iku-dictionary) is excluded as already taught by chapter-15/iku-dict-form, whose note says only 'Dictionary form of いきます ... Regular 1' with nothing about casual speech. In the extras, yeah-im-going (うん、いく) has no note, and going-to-party-tomorrow's note says only that a question 'can end directly on the plain verb with rising intonation, no か needed'.
fix: Add one sentence to the going-to-party-tomorrow or yeah-im-going note: casual speech uses the dictionary form where polite speech uses the ます form (いきます → いく).

claim: The book says を is often omitted in casual speech; no card shows a sentence with を dropped.
evidence: Book: 'は and を are often omitted.' The only mention in the deck is the note on tomodachi-to-iku-casual ('と is never dropped in casual speech, unlike は, を and a destination に'); every extras sentence that drops a particle drops は or に, none drops を.
fix: Add one casual sentence that drops を from a taught polite pattern (for example a casual version of a Lesson 8 'X をたべます' sentence), with a note naming the dropped を.

claim: Two parts of the book's particle-retention rule have no card: で and や are never dropped, and に stays when the sentence involves a benefactive expression.
evidence: Book: 'The particle に is often omitted when indicating a destination, but when the sentence involves someone relating to a benefactive expression, or when it indicates current location, it is not omitted. ... で, と, and や are not omitted.' Carded: current-location に (doko-ni-iru-casual) and と (tomodachi-to-iku-casual, whose note names only と). No card or note covers で, や, or the benefactive に.
fix: Widen the tomodachi-to-iku-casual note to 'と, で and や are never dropped', and either add a casual sentence keeping に with a giving/receiving verb from Lesson 14 or mention it in the doko-ni-iru-casual note.

claim: The book's point that a bare first or last name, or a nickname, can be used with no title at all has no card or note.
evidence: Book: 'The first name or last name without a title, as well as nicknames, are also used.' The dialogue shows it: やまだ: 'あべの?' (Abe with no さん). The suffix-kun and suffix-chan notes say only that くん/ちゃん replace さん; nothing says the title can be dropped.
fix: Add a sentence to the suffix-kun or suffix-chan note: among friends a name is also used bare, with no さん, くん or ちゃん.

claim: The exclusion reason for the いい cell says the extras unit drills casual いい with no です, but no extras card does.
evidence: excludedReason: 'Already taught: chapter-10/ii ... The casual point (no です) only shows in a sentence, which the extras unit drills.' The book's table prints いい as the casual present affirmative. The extras ship よくない (ii-present-neg), よかった (ii-past-aff) and よくなかった (ii-past-neg), but no sentence ending on bare いい; the pattern is shown only for おおきい (kaban-ookii-casual).
fix: Either add a short casual sentence ending on いい (for example このアプリ、いい) or correct the exclusion reason to say the pattern is carried by kaban-ookii-casual.

claim: The English reads すずきさん as someone being addressed, while the note says it is the topic with は dropped, so the card contradicts itself and does not show the book's は-omission.
evidence: Book: 'noun 1 は noun 2 ですか。 → noun 1 は noun 2 ? ... は is often omitted.' Card: target 'すずきさん、せんせい?', English 'Suzuki, are you a teacher?', note 'A casual yes/no question can drop は entirely, leaving just the topic plus rising intonation.'
fix: Change the English to 'Is Suzuki a teacher?' so it matches the note's reading (the hint already marks casual style).

claim: The English 'Tanaka, is he Japanese?' reads as addressing Tanaka about a third person; the Japanese asks whether Tanaka is Japanese.
evidence: Book: 'は ... sometimes becomes って', as in 'ラジャさん、これって ラジャさんの?' (glossed 'Raja, is this yours?', where ラジャさん is the addressee and これって the topic). Card: target 'たなかさんってにほんじん?', English 'Tanaka, is he Japanese?'.
fix: Change the English to 'Is Tanaka Japanese?'.

claim: The romaji 'uun' breaks the pinned macron rule and disagrees with the same word in this chapter's extras, which write 'ūn'.
evidence: casual-no: target 'ううん', pronunciation 'uun'. casual-answer-no-nationality: 'ūn, amerikajin ja nai'; abe-not-mine: 'ūn, ore no ja nai'. src/translate/romajiStyle.js long-vowel-macron: 'Long vowels take a MACRON, never a doubled vowel'.

claim: The English 'Nuh-uh' gives ううん a childish, contradicting tone the book does not; the book glosses it as a plain casual 'No'.
evidence: Book: 'あべ: ううん、おれのじゃない。' glossed 'Abe: No, it's not mine.'; table: 'いいえ → ううん'. Card English: 'Nuh-uh (casual 'no').' The extras render the same word as 'No' and 'Nope'.

claim: The note points the learner at 'the existing にっこう、きれいだね', a card that was trimmed and does not ship.
evidence: Note: 'Contrasts with the existing にっこう、きれいだね — same place, past tense, negated.' Card kirei-dane-1 (にっこう、きれいだね) is excluded: 'Trimmed at gate 2: a third subject for the same きれいだね / きれいだよ pair.'
fix: Drop the note, or point it at a shipping card (このはな、きれいだね).

claim: The card uses いかない, the plain negative of a verb, which neither this chapter nor any earlier unit teaches.
evidence: Book, Casual Style 1, teaches only the casual present affirmative of verbs ('The present affirmative form of verbs is expressed by the dictionary form'). Card: 'おれ、いかない' / 'I'm not going. (male speaker)'. The ledger before this unit has no plain verb negative (no いかない, no ない-form rule); the nearest is the ある note saying its casual negative is ない.
fix: Replace with an affirmative sentence (for example おれもいく) or a noun sentence with じゃない (おれのじゃない is already the book's).

claim: The card uses わからない, a plain verb negative the chapter does not teach and no earlier unit cards.
evidence: Book teaches only さあ (glossed 'I don't know.') and the dictionary form for the present affirmative. Card: 'さあ、わからない' / 'Well... I don't know.' Earlier units teach わかりません and the dictionary form わかる, but no ない-form. The two other さあ sentences were trimmed, so this is the only one.
fix: Either explain わからない in a note as the casual counterpart of わかりません (さあ、わかりません is already a Lesson 2 card), or keep only the book's bare さあ.
